title: Cabinet approves four multitracking projects covering eight Districts in West Bengal, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 410 Kms
subtitle: The total estimated cost of the projects is Rs. 9,450 crore to be completed up to 2030-31
body_text:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved Four projects of Ministry of Railways with total cost of Rs. 9,450 crore approximately. These projects include:
Kharagpur – Bhadrak (Ranital) 4 th Line – 173 km (West Bengal and Odisha) Bhadrak – Haridaspur 4 th Line – 75 km (Odisha) Gummidipundi – Gudur 3 rd and 4 th Line – 90 km (Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu) Cuttack – Paradeep (Badabandha) 3 rd and 4 th Line - 72 km (Odisha)
The increased line capacity will significantly enhance mobility, resulting in improved operational efficiency and service reliability for Indian Railways. These multi-tracking proposals are poised to streamline operations and alleviate congestion. The projects are in line with the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s Vision of a New India which will make people of the region “Atmanirbhar” by way of comprehensive development in the area which will enhance their employment/ self-employment opportunities.
The projects are planned on PM-Gati Shakti National Master Plan with focus on enhancing multi-modal connectivity & logistic efficiency through integrated planning and stakeholder consultations. These projects will provide seamless connectivity for movement of people, goods, and services.
The 04 (Four) projects covering 08 Districts across the states of West Bengal, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, will increase the existing network of Indian Railways by about 410 Kms. The proposed multi-tracking projects will enhance connectivity to approximately 6,448 villages, which are having a population of about 60 lakhs.
The proposed capacity enhancement will improve rail connectivity to several prominent tourist destinations across the country, including Kuldiha Wildlife Sanctuary, Bhitarkanika National Park, Maa Bhadrakali temple, Maa Dhamarai temple, Panchalingeswar Temple, Talsari–Udaypur and Chandipur Beach, Pulicat Lake, Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary, Lord Veeraraghava Perumal Temple, Gada Kujanga Jagannath Temple, Sarala Temple, Dhabaleswar Temple, Lalitgiri (a Buddhist site), etc.
The proposed projects are essential routes for transportation of commodities such as coal, iron ore, cement, iron and steel, container, automobile, food grains, etc. The capacity augmentation works will result in additional freight traffic of magnitude 76 MTPA (Million Tonnes Per Annum). The Railways being environment friendly and energy efficient mode of transportation, will help both in achieving climate goals and minimizing logistics cost of the country, reduce oil import (~13 Crore Litres) and lower CO2 emissions (~65 Crore Kg) which is equivalent to plantation of 2.60 crore trees.
***

enrichment.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved four railway multi-tracking projects worth about Rs. 9,450 crore, spanning West Bengal, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. The projects—Kharagpur-Bhadrak 4th line, Bhadrak-Haridaspur 4th line, Gummidipundi-Gudur 3rd/4th line, and Cuttack-Paradeep 3rd/4th line—will add about 410 km to the rail network across 8 districts and are to be completed by 2030-31. They are expected to enhance connectivity for around 6,448 villages with a population of about 60 lakh, boost freight capacity by 76 MTPA, and improve access to several tourist and pilgrimage sites.
enrichment.context:
The projects are framed under the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, the government's flagship initiative launched in 2021 for integrated, multi-modal infrastructure planning to reduce logistics costs and improve connectivity across transport modes. Multi-tracking (adding 3rd/4th lines) on congested routes is a recurring strategy of Indian Railways to decongest high-traffic corridors, particularly those carrying bulk freight like coal, iron ore, and cement from mineral-rich eastern India (Odisha, West Bengal) to ports and industrial centres, and along the eastern coast corridor connecting Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

Such capacity augmentation is significant for India's freight modal-shift goals, as rail transport is more energy-efficient and lower-emission compared to road freight, aligning with India's climate commitments (e.g., reduced CO2 emissions cited in the release). These approvals are part of a continuing series of CCEA-cleared railway line-doubling/multi-tracking projects announced periodically, which collectively aim to raise the Railways' freight carrying capacity and reduce dependence on road transport for bulk commodities.

prelims_questions.question: The 'PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan', under which recent railway multi-tracking projects have been approved, primarily aims at:
options: Providing direct cash transfers to farmers for infrastructure development
Integrated, multi-modal planning for infrastructure and logistics efficiency
prelims_questions.explanation: PM Gati Shakti is a national master plan for integrated, multi-modal connectivity and logistics efficiency, launched to coordinate infrastructure planning across ministries.

prelims_questions.question: The Kharagpur-Bhadrak and Bhadrak-Haridaspur multi-tracking rail projects approved by the CCEA primarily pass through which states?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the Kharagpur-Bhadrak (Ranital) and Bhadrak-Haridaspur lines run through West Bengal and Odisha.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of rail multi-tracking projects in reducing logistics costs and enhancing freight capacity in India. How does the PM Gati Shakti framework contribute to such integrated infrastructure planning?
Examine the role of railway infrastructure expansion in achieving India's climate and energy efficiency goals, with reference to modal shift from road to rail freight transport.
